title: Duplex in Decatur
kidsText: Two homes you rent out. The bank lends most of the money. Rent pays you each month.
adultText: Two units on a quiet street, both rented to long-term tenants. The bank will carry most of it.

title: Starter Condo
kidsText: A small home near a hospital. Nurses rent it, so it is almost never empty.
adultText: One bedroom near the hospital. Nurses rent it on rotating contracts, so it is rarely empty.

title: Lawn Care Trailer
kidsText: Mowers, a trailer, and eight yards to cut each week. A helper does the work.
adultText: A used trailer, two mowers, and a list of eight weekly customers. You hire a high-schooler to run it.

title: Total Market Index Fund
kidsText: A tiny piece of many companies. It grows a little every month.
adultText: A slice of every big company at once. Slow and boring, it grows a little every month and pays out a sliver of its value.

title: Birchwood Robotics Shares
kidsText: A new robot company. Its price jumps around a lot. Buy low if you can.
adultText: A young company that builds warehouse robots. The price swings; buy low if you can.

title: Vending Machine Route
kidsText: Six snack machines. Fill them on Saturdays and keep the coins.
adultText: Six snack machines in office lobbies. You restock them on Saturdays and keep the coins.

title: Lakeshore Utilities Shares
kidsText: The power company. Nobody gets rich on it, but it pays you a little every month.
adultText: The power company. Nobody gets rich on it, but it pays a dividend every month like clockwork.

title: High-Yield Savings Account
kidsText: A safe place for your money. It grows a tiny bit every month.
adultText: Online bank, no fees, insured. It will never make you rich, but it grows every month and it is there when the furnace dies.

title: Credit Union Savings
kidsText: Keep money safe at the credit union. It grows a tiny bit each month.
adultText: A share account at your credit union. Insured, no fees, open any day. Small growth, but it is your cushion when something breaks.

title: Emergency Fund Account
kidsText: Save money for surprises. Then a broken car is not a big problem.
adultText: A separate account you never touch for fun. Three months of bills in here turns a surprise into an errand.

title: Six-Month CD
kidsText: Let the bank keep your money for a while. It grows and pays you a little.
adultText: A certificate of deposit at a local bank. Locked up for a while, grows a little faster than savings, and pays a small amount monthly.

title: Twelve-Month CD
kidsText: Wait a whole year and the bank pays you more for waiting.
adultText: A one-year certificate at a steady rate. You agree to wait, and the bank pays you for your patience.

title: Credit Union Certificate
kidsText: Save at the credit union for a set time. It grows every month.
adultText: Your credit union's term certificate. Insured, predictable, and a better rate than the savings account down the hall.

title: Large Company Index Fund
kidsText: Own a tiny piece of the 500 biggest companies. It grows over time.
adultText: One fund holds the largest companies in the country. Low fees, no picking winners. It has gone up over every long stretch so far.

title: Target Retirement Fund
kidsText: One fund with lots of stocks and bonds mixed. Slow and steady.
adultText: Stocks and bonds in one fund that rebalances itself. Grows a bit slower than an all-stock fund and swings less.

title: Total World Index Fund
kidsText: A tiny piece of companies all over the world. Many eggs, many baskets.
adultText: Thousands of companies in dozens of countries in one fund. About as diversified as one purchase can be.

title: Dividend Index Fund
kidsText: Many companies that share their profits. It grows and pays you.
adultText: A fund of companies with long records of paying dividends. Steady growth and a payout every month.

title: Growth Index Fund
kidsText: Fast-growing companies in one fund. It can grow quick, and drop too.
adultText: Tech and other fast growers in one low-fee fund. Grows faster than the broad market in good years and falls harder in bad ones.

title: Pinecrest Solar Shares
kidsText: A young solar company. Its price can jump up or fall down fast.
adultText: A small solar panel installer growing fast and losing money. The price can triple or halve. No dividend.

title: Harvest Grocery Shares
kidsText: A big grocery chain. People always buy food, so it pays you each month.
adultText: A regional grocery chain. Slow growth, but people buy groceries in every economy, and it pays a steady dividend.

title: Northgate Bank Shares
kidsText: A bank in your state. It shares some profit with owners every month.
adultText: A regional bank with a long dividend record. Rate changes move the price, but the payout has held for decades.

title: Quantum Leap Biotech Shares
kidsText: A company testing a new medicine. It could win big or lose it all.
adultText: One drug in late trials. If it is approved the shares soar. If not, they crater. A pure bet.

title: Riverside Telecom Shares
kidsText: The phone and internet company. It pays owners a little each month.
adultText: A cable and phone company with steady customers and a generous dividend. The price barely moves.

title: Mobile Home on a Rented Lot
kidsText: A small mobile home you rent out. Rent comes in each month.
adultText: A clean single-wide in a family park. You own the home, rent the lot, and a retired couple pays you rent.

title: Two-Bedroom Ranch House
kidsText: A small house you rent to a family. The bank lends most of the money.
adultText: A brick ranch with a fenced yard in a small town. Low-down loan for investors; a family is ready to sign a lease.

title: Condo by the Community College
kidsText: A small home near a college. Students rent it every year.
adultText: A two-bedroom condo across from the community college. Leases turn over each August, but it never sits empty long.

title: Basement Apartment
kidsText: Fix up your basement and rent it out. A renter pays you each month.
adultText: Finish your walkout basement with a kitchenette and its own door. A traveling nurse wants it as soon as it is done.

title: Foreclosed Bungalow
kidsText: An old house the bank is selling cheap. It needs work but can pay you.
adultText: A bank-owned bungalow with old carpet and a solid roof. Cheap for a reason, and a good rent once it is cleaned up.

title: Garage Apartment
kidsText: A little home on top of a garage. Someone rents it from you.
adultText: A studio above a detached garage behind a rental house. Small, quiet, and easy to keep rented.

title: Duplex Needing Paint
kidsText: Two homes side by side. Paint them and rent both out.
adultText: Side-by-side duplex, both units occupied, both overdue for paint. Rents are below market, so there is room to grow.

title: Cabin Share by the Lake
kidsText: Own part of a lake cabin. Visitors rent it in the summer.
adultText: A one-quarter share of a lakeside cabin rented to vacationers. Great summers, quiet winters, so the cash flow swings.

title: Pressure Washing Side Hustle
kidsText: A power washer cleans driveways and decks. A helper does the jobs.
adultText: A commercial pressure washer and a trailer. Driveways, decks, and storefronts, with a neighbor's son doing the work.

title: Online Used Book Shop
kidsText: Buy old books cheap and sell them online for more.
adultText: Library sale books bought by the box and resold online. A few hours a week of listing and shipping.

title: Gumball and Toy Machines
kidsText: Gumball machines in stores. Kids put in coins, and you get the money.
adultText: Ten gumball and capsule toy machines in restaurants and laundromats. Refill once a month and split coins with the owners.

title: Bounce House Rentals
kidsText: Rent out bounce houses for birthday parties.
adultText: Two inflatable bounce houses rented for parties. Busy every summer weekend, slow in winter.

title: Air Pumps at Gas Stations
kidsText: Air machines for car tires. People pay a little to fill their tires.
adultText: Coin-operated tire inflators at four gas stations. They run themselves; you collect and service them monthly.

title: Food Truck Partnership
kidsText: Own part of a food truck. When it sells tacos, you get some money.
adultText: A half share of a taco truck with a good chef. The loan covers the truck. Busy lunches pay well; a breakdown does not.

title: Online Tutoring Business
kidsText: Help kids with homework online. Parents pay you each month.
adultText: A website, a scheduling app, and two college students who tutor math and reading online. You keep a cut of every session.

title: Mobile Car Detailing
kidsText: Wash and clean cars at people's homes. A helper does the work.
adultText: A vacuum, a buffer, and a water tank in a used van. A part-timer details cars in office parking lots.

title: Dog Walking Route
kidsText: Walk dogs for busy neighbors. A helper walks them after school.
adultText: Twelve regular clients, an app for booking, and a reliable high-schooler. You handle scheduling and payments.
